steps.title: Thaw and wash PBMCs
steps.instruction: Warm 10 mL washing medium (10 % FBS in RPMI‑1640) and 5 mL washing medium containing benzonase (25 U/mL) to 37 °C. Thaw up to 40 × 10⁶ frozen PBMCs in a 37 °C water bath, transfer to the tube with 10 mL washing medium (no benzonase), centrifuge 300 × g for 10 min at room temperature and discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 1 mL warmed benzonase medium, add 4 mL benzonase medium, mix and incubate 5 min at 37 °C. Centrifuge again 300 × g for 10 min at room temperature and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Plate PBMCs with glucose and stimulant
steps.instruction: Sterile‑filter (0.2 µm) culture medium supplemented with either unlabeled glucose or 1,2‑¹³C₂‑D‑glucose, warm to 37 °C. Resuspend the washed PBMC pellet in the warm medium and adjust to 1 × 10⁶ cells per 100 µL. Transfer 5 × 10⁶ cells (≈500 µL) to an ultra‑low‑attachment 6‑well plate, add medium to a final volume of 1.8 mL, incubate 2 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. Add 200 µL PBS (negative control) or 200 µL LPS solution (100 ng/mL) to reach 2 mL total per well, then incubate another 4 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest PBMCs and collect extracts
steps.instruction: Transfer cell suspension to 2 mL Eppendorf tubes, centrifuge 300 × g for 10 min at 4 °C. Transfer supernatant to new tubes and centrifuge 15 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; keep 1 mL supernatant at –80 °C. Shock‑freeze the cell pellet in liquid N₂ for 5 min, then add 100 µL H₂O:ACN (1:1), vortex, incubate on ice 5 min, centrifuge 15 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, and collect 75 µL supernatant as cell lysate; store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Thaw and wash PBMCs for monocytes
steps.instruction: Repeat the thaw‑and‑wash procedure described in step 1 (warm 10 mL washing medium and 5 mL benzonase medium to 37 °C, thaw up to 40 × 10⁶ PBMCs, transfer to washing medium, centrifuge 300 × g 10 min RT, resuspend in benzonase medium, incubate 5 min at 37 °C, centrifuge 300 × g 10 min RT, discard supernatant).

steps.title: Isolate monocytes by MACS negative selection
steps.instruction: Place LS column at –20 °C. Wash cell pellet with 1 mL MACS buffer (0.5 % BSA in PBS + 2 mM EDTA) and transfer to 1.5 mL tubes. Centrifuge 300 × g 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant. Resuspend pellet in 400 µL MACS buffer (for 5 × 10⁶ cells), add 100 µL FcR blocking reagent, add 100 µL biotin‑antibody cocktail, mix and incubate 5 min on ice (2–8 °C). Add 300 µL MACS buffer, then 200 µL anti‑biotin micro‑beads, mix and incubate 10 min on ice. Wash with 1 mL MACS buffer, centrifuge 300 × g 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 500 µL MACS buffer. Place LS column in magnetic separator, pre‑condition with 3 mL MACS buffer, load cell suspension, collect flow‑through (enriched pan‑monocytes). Wash column three times with 3 mL MACS buffer, combine all flow‑throughs. Take 10 µL for cell count, centrifuge remaining cells 300 × g 10 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Plate monocytes with glucose and monensin
steps.instruction: Sterile‑filter (0.2 µm) culture medium containing either unlabeled glucose or 1,2‑¹³C₂‑D‑glucose, warm to 37 °C. Resuspend the monocyte pellet in the warm medium and adjust to ≈8 × 10⁵ cells per 100 µL. Transfer 8 × 10⁵ cells (≈100 µL) to an ultra‑low‑attachment 24‑well plate, add medium to a final volume of 300 µL per well, add 0.3 µL Monensin per well, and incubate 5 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest monocytes and prepare extracts
steps.instruction: Transfer cell suspension to 2 mL Eppendorf tubes, centrifuge 300 × g 10 min at 4 °C. Carefully remove supernatant (do not aliquot all) and centrifuge it 15 000 × g 10 min at 4 °C before LC‑MS analysis. Shock‑freeze the cell pellet in liquid N₂ for 5 min, add 100 µL H₂O:ACN (1:1), vortex, incubate on ice 5 min, centrifuge 15 000 × g 10 min at 4 °C, collect 75 µL supernatant as cell extract and store at –80 °C or on dry ice.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phase A (deactivation solution)
steps.instruction: To make 1 L mobile phase A, add 100 mL 10 mM CH₃COONH₄ stock solution to 900 mL Milli‑Q water, then add 1 mL InfinityLab deactivator additive (final 5 µM). Let rest overnight at room temperature, filter through a 0.2 µm, 47 mm nylon filter (2 µm pore size), and sonicate 5–10 min to degas.

steps.title: Prepare mobile phase B (deactivation solution)
steps.instruction: To make 1 L mobile phase B, add 100 mL 10 mM CH₃COONH₄ stock solution to 900 mL LC‑MS grade acetonitrile, then add 1 mL InfinityLab deactivator additive (final 5 µM). Let rest overnight at room temperature, filter through a 0.2 µm, 47 mm nylon filter (2 µm pore size), and sonicate 5–10 min to degas. Add the buffer stock solution slowly to the acetonitrile and wait 10–15 min before adding the deactivator additive to minimise precipitation.

steps.title: Run HPLC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Condition the analytical HILIC column as recommended, then run a couple of blank injections to verify column conditioning and pressure stability. Inject each sample (≈21 min per run) using the dMRM method described (target analytes and transitions). Use an in‑line filter to protect the column from any precipitate.

steps.title: Prepare stock and QC solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve each standard in acetonitrile:water (1:1) to a concentration of 1 mg/mL, aliquot, and store at –80 °C for use as stock solutions and quality‑control (QC) samples.

description: This protocol can be applied to different cell cultures. Conditions of cell incubation will need previous evaluation and adjustment. We show here, the protocols used for the incubation of PBMCs and monocytes. Two different conditions were used in both cases: with labeled (1,2-13C2-D-glucose) and unlabeled glucose.
